verdict: At the gameplay camera, where nearly all play happens, Act V is clearly below the Acts III/IV floor on both the desktop and the phone. The play frame reads as three flat values cut on a 1 m grid: white snow with half or less of the Field's surface detail and about a quarter of the Woods' (3-5 against 9-10 and 15-17), near-black water and thin ice (16-51% of the desktop frame under 16/255, against 1-4% in the Field and 0-1% in the Woods; inside the Cradle's ring the ice rises only to about 34/255, where the Field's ash reaches about 80), and asphalt-grit flats, all with staircase edges. Dressing is 10-25 times sparser. Rocks look like crumpled paper, cliffs like smooth black walls, bergs like glass gems, holes like black ponds, and the fires are candles that light nothing. Worse for the story, the coast's three states look the same where the player walks: the frozen Landing under the black aurora is only 2-9% darker than at the tide, and the seaLit one is the same frame again. The Freeze cine shows no frozen crests, a lit beam whites out a third of the play frame behind a hard edge, and the occluder dither dissolves the Skerry Light in the Freeze cine because it assumes a south camera. The 2026 moments exist only in the low cines with the sky in them. Stage C's new arrival framing puts the green curtain across the upper third, the true aurora over the Light's skerry and over Whitecliff is striking, the whale, the Icebound Ship and the stilt huts hold up, and after seaLit the green mirror finally reads on the black ice. These beat the Field's own murky low cines, but the ground under them is still the play frame's ground. The black thread in the arrival does not show, and the payoff cine still frames the tower's foot with the lantern off the top while its beam turns half the sky khaki. I found no renderer artefact: the Bayer dither is the game's convention, and the grain on the ice is the shader's stretched noise, absent from the Field under the same swiftshader. The fixes that would lift the act most, in order: frayed edges, readable values on water and ice, distinct frozen and seaLit nights, the aurora on the ground, materials, dressing, fires and beams (distance fade), then the landmarks. (Nothing in the repo was edited; the full list with notes is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-abyssos/848977a8-1632-5f97-b36d-9baf61edd253/scratchpad/act5/look/crit1/out/issues.json and crit1.md.)

issues.where: Both zones, everywhere water, thin ice, thick ice and snow meet: the Landing water (sea.js buildSea/buildIce, build.js buildGround Act V branch, gen5.js Landing beds)
issues.what: Edges follow the 1 m cell grid as 90-degree staircases. The Landing water is a rectangular "swimming pool" with a notched rim, and its waterline is ruler-straight because gen5 shelves the Landing beds by x only, in straight north-south bands (an ASCII dump of seed 3 shows columns 4/3/2/1). The wading water on the flats shows as pale rectangles. The Grey Light islet, the causeway, the bay rim at d.iceShut, the Fall fjord foot, the hole rims and the drowned-light pads all have notched cell edges. The thin ice's lip skirts are vertical cell-edge quads that read as pale steps at the cliff foot (sea.js:784-787); after the Freeze the frozen bay's south lip is one ruler-straight grey plank right across the frame (e-fz-bay2). The water laid under hull footprints shows as navy rectangles sticking out of the snow round the Graveyard hulls. This is the first thing the eye reads in nearly every Act V frame. Acts III and IV have irregular polygon edges.
issues.fix: 1) sea.js shoreJit: jitter EVERY corner where water, thin ice or a deck meets floor or thick ice, not only floor corners that drop to a sea bed below -1 m. Use 0.35-0.45 m of noise, apply it to the ground, water and ice vertices alike, and add a per-pixel noise-warped contour (dep + (n-0.5)*0.12 before the 0.37-0.43 smoothstep, and the same offset in the foam and the G_WET edge) so lines wander inside the cell. 2) Use the farlight's frayed band (aB / G_EDGE) for the thick-ice and snow edge toward OPEN water too: the bay's north rim, the islets, the road ends and the hole rims. 3) Drop the vertical lip skirts and fray those edges like the others. 4) Cover only the cells under a hull's real outline with water, or fray the footprint's outer ring. 5) gen5 dressing (no layout rule involved): give the Landing water's bed bands an fbm-warped x (bed from x + 4*fbm), still quantised to 0.15, and re-run check-act5.

issues.where: Coast: open and closed water, the Fall shelf, the Graveyard bay. Farlight: every thin-ice field, lead and hole (sea.js water colour :241, thin-ice body :608)
issues.what: Closed water, thin ice and open leads are all near-black: linear 0.002-0.02 before ACES. At the play camera 34-51% of the Graveyard frame, 41% at the Grey Light, 35% on the Fall shelf, 31% at the bay rim and 16-21% on the Ice Road is under 16/255. The Field of Ash is at 1-4% and the Weeping Woods at 0-1% (all desktop, quality 2). On the phone at quality 1 the Field's unlit ash also falls to 22-41% black, but there the black lies outside the Cradle's light, and inside the ring the ash is lit and textured. In Act V the ring lifts the black ice under the hero only to about 34/255 (the Field's lit ash inside its ring is about 80), and two metres outside it the ice falls to RGB 2,5,10, on the very surface the player must read as walkable or deadly (e-fz-iceroad). The cause on the water is measurable: it is a MeshBasicMaterial lit only in its own shader, and at the play pitch (54 degrees down) Schlick's F is about 0.02. The sky term uSkyC*(0.03+0.5F) therefore adds about 0.002-0.004 linear, and the closed water ends near 0.01. Walkable thin ice and deadly open water read as the same black void, because only the faint brash and the static streaks tell them apart. The hole's pitch-black pond and the black field round it merge (d-f-hole1). This is also why the act feels empty and flat.
issues.fix: Lift the thin-ice body to a readable steel blue-grey (linear about 0.02-0.05, so 35-60/255 after ACES) with visible bubbles and cracks and a stronger sky sheen. Lift closed and open water to a night teal (0.012-0.03) with a moving moon and sky sheen. Make open water the darkest surface, and make it read by its motion (ripple glints, a slow swell highlight, sea smoke) rather than by being black. Keep the 0.45 m wading step as a colour change, not a fall to black. Check against the Field of Ash: its darkest walkable ground sits near 30/255.

issues.where: Both zones, the act's signature image ("put the sky on the floor"): the water and ice mirror (sea.js vAur), the ground's G_AUR (build.js:1331), the cine dome (sea.js auroraSky :874, :907)
issues.what: The aurora is barely in the game. In the water it is one blurred horizontal green-violet stripe at a fixed screen height in every water view, not curtains (p-shallows-high, p-sealight-grey-lit-high). On the snow it is invisible, because G_AUR adds 0.06. Under the black aurora (the frozen coast, the whole Farthest Light before seaLit) the ice and water mirror nothing. In the cines, the dome's curtain hems sit 4-14 degrees up, so only the low cines (the arrival and the Light lit, both pitch 0.12) frame them well. The story's cines at pitch 0.22-0.3 (the Freeze, the Skotos rising, the naming, the farlight arrival) frame only a sliver of curtain along the top edge (p-frz-bay-cine, e-frz-bay-cine). After seaLit the mirror does show at the play camera as a soft green-violet swath on the black ice, on the Farthest Light's fields and on the frozen bay (p-fl-camp, e-sl-iceroad). This reads and is the best moment of the mirror, though it is still one blurred band. The coast's frozen sea under the true aurora stays a dull teal plane even in a low cine with the green curtain overhead (p-sl-overlook-cine).
issues.fix: Water: per pixel at q>=1 within ~20 m of the camera, less blur (2-3 m, not +6 m), the ripple normal breaking the curtains into moving streaks, and the arcs' direction varying with x so the stripe becomes curtains. Ground: G_AUR at 0.15-0.25 on snow, as ribbons drifting across, with a faint green sheen on the ice and snow facing the sky. Black aurora: draw it as moving black-violet curtains that occlude the stars and the sky sheen in the mirror, so the Freeze reads as something happening, not nothing. Dome: drop the hems to 1-6 degrees and let the dome show up to pitch 0.45, so every story cine at 0.22-0.34 frames the curtains.

issues.where: Coast after the Freeze and after seaLit, at the play camera: the Landing, the strand, the Shallows and Skerry Bay under the black and the true aurora (atmos.js coastFrozen :29, coastAurora :36 against coast :28)
issues.what: Nothing in the play frame says the sea has frozen and the sky has gone black. coastFrozen differs from coast only by hemi 0.85 to 0.75, moonI 1.0 to 0.9 and a slightly bluer moon. With the correct atmosphere forced, the frozen Landing is only 9% darker than the tide one on the desktop, with the same hue (centre mean RGB 187,182,180 against 206,206,200; e-fz-camp against d-camp-lit), and 2% darker on the phone (p-fz-camp against p-camp-lit). The huts, the snow and the people are lit as before. The black aurora is above the frame at pitch 0.95, and its mirror on the ice is black on black. The Shallows keep their tide by design and stay the same asphalt flats (p-frz-shallows, p-fz-bay). The design asks for the Skotos "darkening the world": uAurDark up, the fog eased toward black and a global light gain (design table row 15). After seaLit (coastAurora = coast with aur 1) the true aurora is not in the play frame either: the camp, the bay and the Shallows are the same frames again (mean absolute difference 6.5/255 between the frozen and the seaLit camp, mostly people moving; p-sl-camp, p-sl-bay, p-sl-shallows). The three states of the act's home look alike wherever the player walks.
issues.fix: Make coastFrozen a different night: hemi about 0.45, moonI about 0.55 with a cold violet-blue moon (0x8c96d8), the sky and ground colours toward violet-black, the fog toward 0x05060c at density about 0.028, and exposure about 1.05. Then let the hero's warm pool, the lit hearth and the sea-lights carry the frame: they become the only warm light, which is the act's point. Add slow black bands drifting across the snow and ice in play (a world-space noise mask times uAurDark on the ground and ice, about 10% darkening), so the black aurora is felt without looking up. Rime the hut roofs, boats and racks after the Freeze (a frost tint on the shared materials driven by uFreezeAll). For coastAurora, tint the hemisphere light and the snow toward the aurora green (sky 0x5a8a78 as in farlightAurora, hemi about 0.95), and put the green on the snow, not only in the water, so the morning after reads as a change.

issues.where: Both zones' sky in the cines: the aurora dome's curtains (sea.js auroraSky :866-885) and the colour of the "true" aurora (sea.js:30 uAurCol, never written)
issues.what: The dome draws its curtains as a single even band of the same height and brightness right across the sky, with its lower edge parallel to the horizon. It reads as a theatre curtain hung over the scene, the same on the coast, the Farthest Light and over Whitecliff after seaLit (d-fl-arena-low, p-overlook-cine, d-town-north-low, where its saturated green also fights the warm village). It has no folds turning toward the viewer, no corona overhead and no bright white-green lower hem with violet tops. uAurCol is a constant green that nothing writes, so the "true aurora" after seaLit (design: green and white) differs from the first green one only by brightness (aur 1 against 0.8). The black aurora (d-f-arena-low) is the more convincing of the two.
issues.fix: Give the curtains depth: vary the hem's elevation strongly with azimuth (some folds dipping to the horizon, some arching overhead), modulate brightness along the curtain (bright knots, gaps), add a faint second layer higher up and a corona when the camera looks north and up, and make the lowest hem a sharp white-green line with the rays fading upward to violet. Write uAurCol from the atmosphere (a key like aurCol in ATMOS): green on the coast, greener-white for the true aurora, then animate toward white at the front.

issues.where: Coast arrival cine, the act's first image (story.js coastArrival :1149, now o.z-5, pitch 0.12, zoom 0.85, coastCine; the black thread uAurDark 0.15), and every Act V cine over the Landing
issues.what: Stage C's new framing (story.js changed at 06:18) fixes the sky: the green curtain now fills the upper third and is the best thing in the act (arr/p-arrival-cine). The ground half below it has not changed. It shows a flat grey asphalt plain for the flats, the Landing water as a flat teal-grey slab with a stepped rectangular outline and a ruler-straight right edge, and a black obelisk with a white skirt dead centre. Around it stand paper-snow shark-fin stacks, two flat-topped table mesas behind, the Frozen Fall as a pale glass panel on a black wall, and the sea-light towers as grey stubs. The design's beat "a black thread runs through the curtains at the northern edge and is gone" (uAurDark 0.15) does not read. The dome only desaturates and dims about 8% overall (sky mean G 55 to 50, 3% of sky pixels change by more than 20/255), with no thread shape (arr/p-arrival-thread against arr/p-arrival-cine). The old framing (coast/p-arrival-cine) and the other cines over the Landing (camp, Grey Light, bay) show the same ground: a flat teal plane, a hard horizon and shark-fin stacks.
issues.fix: Fix the ground through the edge, flats, rock and cliff issues, then: take the obelisk down (gen5 rock islet height), give seaBeyond swell-lit wave normals and a moon path, add a horizon haze band (fog to the sky colour over the last 30 m) and low headland and island silhouettes in the fog. For the thread, draw it as a shape, not a global dim: a narrow dark ribbon (a band mask in elevation and azimuth, a few degrees wide) that crosses the curtains' hem from the north and eats them as it passes. Drive it through a separate uniform (say uAurThread 0-1), so the 0.15 is not spread over the whole dome.

issues.where: Coast: the Freeze cine (story.js:1388, B.z+14, pitch 0.22; sea.js uFreezeAll, the swell :125-126, freezeAt)
issues.what: The design's image 7 ("waves stop mid-crest and turn to ice while three beams sweep over them") does not read. Half-way through (uFreezeAll 0.55, the story's own framing) the bay's water is a flat, smooth, pale grey-green plane with stepped corners. No crest stands up, because the swell is two 25 m sines of 0.06-0.18 m, invisible at cine distance. No frost pattern or racing white front reads at that distance, and the aurora overhead is still green (e-frz-bay-cine). Seen from the play camera (e-frz-shallows), the frozen water is a flat light-grey sheet printed with a repeating squiggle pattern (the frost lines from tNoise at P*0.6), like linoleum, with cell-stepped edges. This is the act's turning point.
issues.fix: Give the Freeze its own wave field: short steep crests (wavelength 3-6 m, 0.3-0.6 m high, sharpened) grown in over the first second, then caught. Make the crests white with rime and spray frozen in the air (fx shards held still), and the troughs dark. Drive a bright, glittering front band 2-3 m wide from the shore outward, visible at 20 m. Darken the dome's curtains in step with uAurDark (the story eases it to 1). Fray the stepped corners (see the edge issue).

issues.where: Story cines: the landmark a cine frames dissolves into the occluder dither (story.js cines without occ; boot.js:289 village.update(pl.x, pl.z); build.js occlude and Village.update)
issues.what: The dither that keeps the hero visible is computed from the hero's position with a fixed play-camera direction (south, slope 1.25), not from the real camera. In a low cine that looks from somewhere else, a tall prop just south of the hero still dissolves. In the Freeze cine at the story's own framing (B.z+14, pitch 0.22, the hero at the boss spot where the Walking Tower fight ends), the Skerry Light, the lit landmark of the shot, is a Bayer mesh from its base to its lantern room. This happens on the phone and on the desktop (p-frz-bay-cine, e-frz-bay-cine). Any low shot with the hero just north of a tower does the same (e-fz-iceroad-cine). Only the Light-lit cine (story.js:1668) passes occ: { z: -999 }; the arrival, rite, Freeze, Skotos-rise and naming cines do not, and the houses' fade (Village.update) ignores occ entirely. The mechanism is shared (in a low shot of mine, the Weeping Woods dither every willow round the hero too, cmp/p-weep-mere-cine), and in Act V it strikes the very landmark a story cine is about.
issues.fix: Requests to story.js: pass occ: { z: -999 } (or the shot's real occluder point) on every Act V cine that frames a landmark (:1149, :1196, :1388, :1501, :1648). Request to boot.js: pass the same occ point to village.update, so houses and towers obey it too. Better, in build.js: test the real segment from the hero to R.cam's position against each fade footprint and height, so the dither follows the camera in any shot.

issues.where: Farlight: the payoff cine, the Farthest Light lit (story.js:1668: target FL.z+6, pitch 0.12, zoom 0.95; a framing request to stage C), and its look (build5 farLight/lanternRoom, beamMesh)
issues.what: Worked out from the cine camera (updateCamera): the camera sits about 7.6 m up and 20 m south of the tower, and the frame's top edge is at +12 degrees. The lantern room and its fire are at about +23 degrees, so the moment the Light is lit shows the tower's plain grey foot. The lantern, the beam's origin and most of the returning aurora are out of frame. A capture at the story's exact framing on the phone (arr/p-payoff-cine) confirms it: the shaft runs off the top of the frame with no lantern. The Light's own beam, swept toward the camera, turns the whole right half of the sky and sea a flat khaki-grey (sky mean 112,110,95 right of the tower against 15,62,45 left of it; crops/p-payoff-right.png), so a muddy wash cuts the returning green curtain in two. (The fine dither on the tower's foot in that capture comes from my harness: the real scene passes occ.) My cine at pitch 0.2 (d-fl-arena-cine) shows the same: the shaft runs off the top, a hard-edged pale cone crosses the sky, and the sea beyond is a flat teal plane with a ruler horizon. The aurora's green on the ice is the one strong element.
issues.fix: Request to story.js: frame the lighting from farther and lower, so the lantern sits in the upper third and the curtains above it: target FL.z+20, pitch about 0.02-0.06, lookY about 9, zoom about 1.6. Or tilt up mid-scene with a later G.cine pitch step. On the look side: a bright lantern room with a halo and lens flare, a soft-edged beam with dust (see the beam issue), the tower's texture as weathered stone (not birch bark), and the far sea lit by the beam and mirroring the true aurora.

issues.where: Both zones: dressing density (gen5.js dressCoast and the farlight's fields, build5.js act5Level)
issues.what: The act is nearly empty. Seed 3 has 1.7 props per 100 m2 of floor on the coast and 0.9 on the Farthest Light, against 21.8 in the Field of Ash and 52.3 in the Weeping Woods. Most play frames are a white sheet, a black void and the hero. The Landing has five huts and two racks but no nets, crates, barrels, fish, sledges, ropes, firewood stacks or tracks. The Farthest Light's camp is a thick-ice disc with an Act IV brazier and the waypoint, and nothing else. The Ice Road looks the same along its whole length.
issues.fix: Add an instanced dressing pass (about 8-15 props per 100 m2 of floor). On land: snow-buried rocks and tufts. At the Landing: nets, crates, casks, fish racks, firewood, sledges and a cooking frame. On the flats: drift-buried wreck timber. On the farlight: ice rubble, pressure slabs, frozen spray and cracks, abandoned gear and the keepers' old cairn-poles. At the farlight camp: tents, furs, sledges, crates and a rope line to the ship. Keep all of it on blocked or decorative spots, with no layout rule touched. Draw it from its own RNG (seed ^ a constant), as the Neck's corridor does, so the layout and the packs stay identical, and re-run check-act5.

issues.where: Both zones: all snow ground, the Landing, the strand, the Farthest Light's camp and road (rime/snow layer, G_GLINT drifts in build.js:1397)
issues.what: The snow is flat, untextured-looking white. Measured surface detail (mean |image - 6 px blur| at the screen centre) is 3-5 on the coast's snow against 9-10 in the Field of Ash and 15-17 in the Weeping Woods. There are no sastrugi, tracks, tufts, stones or soot round the huts. The snowTrod path is salt-and-pepper noise, and the bare thick ice on the road shows the ice layer's Voronoi as blue crazy paving at a small tile.
issues.fix: Strengthen the snow's normal (the rime/snow normal at x2 scale plus a macro wind-ripple normal). Raise the drift contrast in G_GLINT from 0.8-1.06 to about 0.6-1.12, and orient the drifts round obstacles, with darker blue AO pools within 1-2 m of every prop and cliff foot. Add sparse dark accents: grass tufts poking through, stones, animal tracks. Replace or rescale snowTrod with a softer trodden snow at a larger tile. Scale the ice layer up x3 on thick ice and mostly bury it under snow.

issues.where: Coast: the tidal flats (the Shallows, the Graveyard shore) and Skerry Bay's arena floor (rime/shore layer, ground5 in build.js:1096)
issues.what: The shore layer (low_tide_rocks at a 2.4 m tile) renders as uniform pixel-scale grit, like asphalt or a road surface, at both tides. The Walking Tower's arena is an asphalt bowl with three perfect snow circles (the islets, r 3.5), each holding one boulder: it reads as golf bunkers. At high tide the wading flats are this same grit under faint grey water. After the Freeze the bay floor keeps the same asphalt bands in a figure of eight round the islets, now between snow (p-fz-bay, p-fz-bay-cine).
issues.fix: Re-pack the shore layer from wet sand or shingle with ripple marks at a larger scale (two to three times), and mix in a second macro read: darker wet patches, ripple bands following the bed contours, rock-pool blots. In gen5's dressing, scatter shingle bands, shell and kelp lines along the wrack line, and small rock clusters. Noise-warp the islets' snow discs so they are not circles. In pack-rime, keep the credits when the source changes.

issues.where: Coast and farlight, in play and in the cines: a lit beam sweeping near or toward the camera (sea.js beamMesh :929)
issues.what: When the beam passes near or through the play camera's view, it becomes a flat, pale, translucent wedge with hard straight edges covering about a third of the screen and washing out the scene (p-sealight-grey-lit). In Skerry Bay at the play camera, the Skerry Light's beam whites out the right third of the frame behind a hard diagonal edge, turns a rock inside it into a flat sepia ghost and makes the quest tracker's white text unreadable (e-fz-bay). Seen from above, the shell's silhouette is a ruler-straight vertical line across the ice with a pale wash on one side (e-sl-iceroad, crops/e-sl-iceroad-wedge.png). Seen from afar in a cine it is a hard-edged cone. Swept toward the camera in the payoff cine, it turns half the sky and sea khaki-grey (arr/p-payoff-cine). The alpha depends only on N.V of a DoubleSide shell and on the length, with no fade by distance to the camera.
issues.fix: Fade the cone by camera distance (smoothstep 3-12 m) and by the eye's height inside it. Soften the silhouette with a radial falloff from the axis in the cone's local space instead of the shell's N.V. Add slowly drifting dust noise inside the cone, and cut its intensity at the play pitch (it should glow, not paint). Keep the motes.

issues.where: Coast and farlight: every rock, sea-stack, rock face, shore rock, boulder and skerry rock (build.js worldMat snow :197, the cliff5 material in build5.js:40)
issues.what: Rocks look like crumpled white paper. The worldMat snow mask is a hard smoothstep(0.45, 0.8) on the face normal, so whole facets snap to pure white and the rest to near-black. The rock texture underneath disappears, and the result is a black-and-white camouflage pattern on every stack and boulder (den, jetty, the bay's three boulders, every sea-stack in the cines).
issues.fix: Drive the snow from a smoothed normal (vertex normal or a blurred world-normal), soften the ramp (0.55-0.95), keep 30-40% of the rock colour showing through thin snow, tint the snow's shadow side blue-grey, and add noise breakup at 0.3 m, not 3 m. For sea-stacks, use the coastCliff and rockFace scans or several stacked rocks, not one boulder stretched 2.6x tall (its texture streaks vertically).

issues.where: Coast: the cliffs round the cove, the Neck, the ebb caves, the Fall fjord, the strand. Farlight: the south headlands (gen5.js heights() :587, build.js wall projection :1380)
issues.what: The cliffs are smooth dark sheets that rise 8-18 m within 3 cells of the floor and follow the cell outline. The seaCliff layer is projected sideways, so it smears into horizontal or vertical streaks and stair stripes. From the play camera they read as soft grey ramps. In the cines (arrival, camp, bay) they read as untextured black walls, a giant black obelisk (a rock islet raised to cliff height) and flat-topped table mesas on the horizon. From the overlook after the Freeze, two smooth black walls fill about 40% of the phone frame (p-fz-overlook-cine). From the Graveyard, one smooth grey wall with a rounded top fills half the frame, like a tarp (e-fz-graveyard-cine).
issues.fix: Shape the rock with fbm ledges and terraces, and ramp the base over 2-3 cells. Displace the ridge line by 2-4 m of fbm for silhouettes, and keep isolated rock islets low (4-6 m) and rounded. Project the wall layer triplanar at a larger scale with a vertical strata normal, and dust ledges with snow by slope. Hide the cell-following foot with more rockFace and coastCliff scans and scree.

issues.where: Coast: the Landing hearth (lit and unlit). Farlight: the fire-cairns. Both: the sea-lights' fire cages and lantern rooms (build5.js hearth :712, fireCage :570, lanternRoom :622)
issues.what: Act V's fires are a flameMesh (two small glow cones and a halo sprite) with no fire, ember or smoke emitter. The lit hearth reads as a small yellow smudge in a ring of white chips under a black tripod-and-chain glyph, and it lights nothing: the huts and the people round it stay snow-blue (p-camp-lit, p-camp-lit-cine). The sea-light's fire on a 9 m tower is a candle in a birdcage. The Field of Ash's camp brazier pushes an fx 'fire' emitter and a strong warm light (build.js:2463), and it is the warm heart of its frame. The rite, the first time the word Skotos is spoken in the game, is staged round this hearth. On the phone, the Farthest Light's camp brazier (build5 brazier) is a glowing ball on a black tripod, and the occluder dither runs over it: the camp's only fire becomes a sphere of Bayer pixels (p-fl-camp, crops/p-fl-brazier.png). The Landing's lantern posts do the same: the post and its glow disc turn into a dotted ring whenever the hero passes north of them (e-fz-jetty, crops/e-jetty-post.png).
issues.fix: Push fx 'fire' plus 'embers' and a thin smoke column for the hearth (s 1.0-1.2), the cairns (0.7) and the sea-light cages (0.9) while lit (setLit can add or remove an emitter on the zone's list through userData). Scale the flame up two to three times, with three or four flame cards and a flicker. Light the hearth with a warm PointLight (range 10-12) that reaches the huts. Request to light.js (stage C): the pool's light intensity for the hearth in 'sea' zones should warm the huts round it. Give the hearth a pot and stones that read, and drop the thin chain glyph. Exempt fires and emissive props from the occluder dither (they never hide the hero), or dither only their non-emissive parts.

issues.where: Farlight: the Farthest Light on the core, the boss arena's centrepiece (build5.js farLight :697; gen5 places it at the core's south edge)
issues.what: With the hero on the north half of the core (where the keepers stand and the fight centres), the 15.5 m shaft stands between the camera and the hero. A coarse 4x4-Bayer-dithered grey cylinder then covers the middle third of the screen (a quarter of the phone frame, p-f-core). Its hollow top is seen from above as a ring with brown patches, and the door-stone is a grey box with a row of LED dashes (d-f-farlight, d-f-core). The dither is the game's convention for houses, but at this size, in the boss fight, it hides the fight.
issues.fix: For tall act props (the Farthest Light, the sea-light towers, the Walking Tower's island light), cut the shaft above about 3 m (a clipping plane or an alpha cut-away with a soft edge) while the hero is inside its occlusion cone, instead of dithering the whole tower, or fade it to 20-25% with a smooth alpha. Cap the shaft's top so it is never seen hollow.

issues.where: Farlight: the Light's Skerry arena (the Skotos fight) in its cine and at play, under the black aurora (build5 farLight, gen5 core/ring/cross, atmos farlight)
issues.what: The final arena reads as a diagram: a pale cross and ring drawn on black, with a plain grey cylinder planted on a flat disc in the middle (no base rock, door, lantern-room glow or snow on it), four toy cairns and paper rocks. Behind it are a flat black sea and a black sky. The black aurora is only a grey smudge at the top edge (d-f-arena-cine, p-f-arena-cine). The skerry is not a rock island: its core is a flat snow disc. Nothing says the Skotos is near: no darkness moving under the ice, no sea smoke at the ice edge, no torn black curtains overhead.
issues.fix: Make the core a real rock skerry: raised rock ledges round the core (a rockPile ring, the base set's rock scans in the cliff stone), snow drifts, and the keepers' old stones and offerings. Seat the tower on a stepped stone base with a lit door and a glowing lantern room even when dark (a dim ember). Under the black aurora, draw the sky as moving black curtains with violet edges that blot the stars, and have uShade slot 3 sweep slowly under the arena's ice. Push sea smoke off the open sea north of the arena. Light the ring and the cross with frost glints so they read as ice paths, not paint.

issues.where: Farlight: the bergs (build5.js bergGeo :497, the icy material :54)
issues.what: The bergs are low-poly icosahedron domes, flat-shaded (toNonIndexed) and wrapped in the ice layer's caustic and Voronoi pattern like a swimming-pool texture, with a bright Phong specular blob in the middle at q2. They read as glass gems or blue boulders, not icebergs: no snow cap, no sheer calved faces, no strata, no rubble at the foot. On the phone a berg fills the top of the frame as one giant faceted glass gem (p-f-berg1). When the hero is behind one, a flat grey rectangle (the terrain rise under it) shows inside the dithered dome.
issues.fix: Smooth the normals (keep the geometry indexed and computeVertexNormals). Build bergs from three to five intersecting slabs with near-vertical calved faces and a flat snow-capped top. In icyMat, use a world-space vertical strata noise, a white opaque core with blue only in cracks and hollows, and snow on top (ysn from a smoothed normal). Drop the Phong blob or make it a fresnel rim. Put ice rubble round the foot. The terrain rise under each berg (gen5 bergH, drawn as ROCK in the seaCliff wall layer) shows as a grey rock monolith whenever the berg dithers (d-f-hole1-cine, d-f-berg2): draw the ground under berg cells in the icy look, or keep the rise a metre under the dome everywhere.

issues.where: Farlight: the Breathing-holes, the leads and the ice edge (sea.js SEA_LOW brash :248-251, fx.js seasmoke)
issues.what: A Breathing-hole is a big pitch-black pond whose rim is a camouflage pattern of dark-grey blobs (the brash, a thresholded 12 m noise). There is no slush, no floes, no glint and no lamplight on the water. The leads and the ice edge are flat black bands with the same camo pattern along stepped edges. These are the act's objectives (sealing the holes), and they read as holes in the render. After 45 frames of waiting (p-f-hole0-wait, crops/p-hole0-smoke.png), the sea smoke is four or five faint round grey blobs sitting on the black water, evenly spaced and still: out-of-focus dots, not rising vapour. Where the Cradle's warm pool reaches the hole's lip, the vertical ice skirts show as lit orange rectangles.
issues.fix: Brash as plates: a Voronoi of 0.3-1.2 m cells with dark gaps, bobbing on the swell. Grease ice as a grey sheen band along edges. Sea smoke as wisps: tall, stretched, curling sprites (2-4x taller than wide, noise-eroded alpha), rising 2-4 m, drifting with the wind and fading at the top, with many more of them along the lip than in the middle, so the hole reads as breathing. Give the black water the moon's and lamps' glints and a slow swell highlight, and put broken-ice floes at the hole's edge from the floe pool.

issues.where: Farlight after the seals: a sealed Breathing-hole and its lead (sea.js freeze rime :308-318, the water held frozen at aFrz)
issues.what: A sealed hole and its lead become a flat pale-grey slab printed with a small, repeating "frost feather" pattern, with rectangular cell steps at its edges. They read as a paved plaza dropped into the ice, not as new sea ice (d-fl-hole1). On the phone, the plaza's 1 m steps and the marker beam's wedge (a quarter of the frame) are the first things you see (p-fl-hole1). The marker light's short beam crosses the frame as a hard white wedge.
issues.fix: New ice should read as dark, glassy and clear (darker than the old snowed ice, with a few white feather blooms and pressure cracks at the lead's edges), and fade into the old ice over a ragged band. Scale the feather pattern up and break its repetition with a second octave. Fray the edges (see the edge issue). Give the marker beam the same distance and silhouette fade as the sea-light beams (see the beam issue).

issues.where: Farlight: the Ice Road's pressure ridges, the ice blocks round footprints, the marker poles (gen5 ridges :1005, build5 iceBlock :323, the icy material's colour :82)
issues.what: The pressure ridges are scattered single lumps of rock scans in the icy material. Its colour (linear 0.008-0.14) makes them read as lead-grey rocks, not ice slabs, and as dots, not ridges. The road looks the same along its whole length: a pale strip, grey lumps and black voids with static (d-f-pole2, pole6, pole10). Each pole's block is a white cube at its foot.
issues.fix: Build ridges from tilted, overlapping slabs (thin boxes or the slab-cut scans), two to five per segment and pushed up at angles, with snow in the gaps. Make the icy colour a pale blue-white with blue-green only in cracks and undersides (about 3x brighter). Vary the road: drifts across it, a wrecked sledge, a frozen-in barrel, the keepers' cairns, a crack field. Replace the pole's cube with three small ice blocks and a snow mound.

issues.where: Farlight: the Drowned Lights' windows and their lanterns (build5 iceWindow :801, sea.js ICE_WINDOW rim :687 and the uGlow under the ice); the coast's sea-light windows
issues.what: Each Drowned Light is a 2x2 dark skylight with cross-shaped muntins (the rim is computed per cell from fract(P), so the inner cell edges draw a cross), on a pale snow pad. A diffuse orange wash lies on the black ice 2-4 m away, attached to nothing visible. No lantern shape and no point of light read through the ice (d-f-drowned0/1/2). The coast's sea-light windows have the same skylight look: in the cines, each tower's foot has a dark four-pane basement window lying on the snow (e-fz-grey-cine, e-fz-fall-cine).
issues.fix: Compute the window rim from the distance to the 2x2 square's outline, not per cell, and fray it irregularly. Draw the lantern as a visible small shape under the window: a bright point with a cross-shaped glint and refraction ripples. Move the glow to the window (the B2b request to gen5: lantern 1 m north of the window centre), or cast it from the window itself as god-rays up through the pane.

issues.where: Coast: the two ebb caves (gen5.js caves :243, bed :324)
issues.what: The ebb caves are not caves. Each is a smooth V half-pipe cut into the south shore, with an octagonal tide pool and a ruler-straight 3-cell canal to the sea. There is no roof, no mouth, no darkness, no dripping and no kelp: it is a skate bowl (p-cave1-high).
issues.fix: Dress each cave with an overhang: a rime rockFace or coastCliff arch north of the cave cells as a lintel, cut away like the houses when the hero is under it. Darken the ground inside (vertex AO 0.35-0.5) and add icicles on the lip, kelp and barnacles. Noise-warp the canal's segment and the pool's disc (dressing only; re-run check-act5).

issues.where: Coast: the Frozen Fall and its pool and icicles (build5.js fallCode :442, icicle :271)
issues.what: The Fall is a faceted pale-blue glass sheet: non-indexed triangles with flat normals and the ice layer's caustic pattern. The icicle clusters lie flat on the Fall's face (not hanging from a lip) as pinkish-beige blobs with dark spikes, like dead fish stuck to glass (crops/p-fall-brown.png). The frozen pool shows the ice layer's Voronoi as swimming-pool tiles (p-fall). This is a named landmark, with a sea-light beside it. In a low cine after the Freeze it reads as a curtain of hard blue facets on a black wall, with the icicles still stuck on its face and the sea-light's beam slicing across it as a pale wedge (e-fz-fall-cine).
issues.fix: Index the rows and computeVertexNormals for smooth bulging columns, and add vertical streak noise with opaque white cores and blue only in the depths (the ICY_GLOW path). Hang the icicles from the cliff lip above the columns: build5 icicle walks out to where the rock stands at p.y, and on the Fall it finds the Fall's own face. Tint them white-blue and translucent-looking with a fresnel rim, not the dark icy colour with a snow cap. Give the pool thick-ice, snow-dusted edges and a smooth clear centre, not the tiled layer.

issues.where: Coast: the Grey Light's islet, the bay islets, every refuge islet (gen5 refuges, sea.js shore foam)
issues.what: The islets are flat snow plates with notched cell edges, lying in a black void. They have no rock, no thickness, no surf or foam where the sea meets them, and no wet band (p-sealight-grey). The Cradle ring hangs over black water at their edge.
issues.fix: Ring each islet with low rocks (rockPile, as the skerry has). Draw foam and a wet dark band wherever water meets land, at any depth: today foam only appears at the tidal waterline, but it also belongs at the islet edges where the depth jumps. Fray the plate's edge (see the edge issue).

issues.where: Both zones, every frame: the hero's Cradle ring on snow (light.js heroRing takes build.js act4Prop lightRing :2753: ringTexture, additive, opacity 0.55, toneMapped false; r 4 in Act V)
issues.what: The ring is the Act IV ground decal, additive and not tone-mapped, drawn at opacity 0.55 with a bright rim. On white snow it reads as a UI selection circle round the hero and is the brightest shape on screen (e-fz-camp, p-f-berg1). Over black water and black ice it floats as a brown halo with a sharp outer edge. On the Field of Ash's dark ground the same ring reads as firelight.
issues.fix: In build.js (ours), give lightRing a snow-friendly ringTexture: falloff from about 0.4 to 1.0 of the radius and a faint, thin rim, and let it be tone-mapped. Request to light.js (stage C): in 'sea' zones, call setOpacity with about 0.2-0.25 and setColor with a deeper amber, and let the PointLight do the work. Keep the gameplay edge readable as a thin, faint, flickering rim.

issues.where: Coast and farlight thin ice: the wind-drift dusting (sea.js ice drift :671-681)
issues.what: The drifts on the black ice are grainy horizontal smears of stretched noise, all running exactly east-west everywhere. They read as TV static or scan lines over every thin-ice field (crops/smoke-zoom.png, d-f-drowned1, e-fz-iceroad2). The cause is the shader's noise stretch (x*0.012 against z*0.045), not the renderer: the Field of Ash under the same swiftshader has no such grain.
issues.fix: Make the drift streaks follow a slowly varying wind direction (rotate the sampling with fbm). Use a smooth low-frequency mask times a fine sparkle instead of thresholded stretched noise, lower its contrast on the black ice, and fade it with camera distance.

issues.where: Coast: the Landing's stilt huts (build5.js stiltHut :383)
issues.what: The stilt huts' roofs are untextured pure-white prisms in the plain 'lam' material with snow 2.4. Next to the textured shack's roof they read as paper boxes (p-camp-unlit, p-huts2, p-fz-camp).
issues.fix: Draw the roof in planks5 or a turf or thatch material, with snow from a normal-driven mask (the worldMat snow path), so the planks or turf show at the eaves and edges. Add icicles on the eaves.

issues.where: Coast: the Ship Graveyard's broken boats (build5 brokenBoat :263, rime brokenBoat scan)
issues.what: The broken boat is a beige pill or zeppelin shape with a flat white patch at one end (an untextured or cut face). Lying on black ice it reads as a capsule, not a wreck (p-graveyard1, d-graveyard1/3).
issues.fix: Check the scan's cut face, then fill or texture it, or cap it with planks. Sink it 0.3 m into the ice, tilt it 15-25 degrees, and add snow on its upper side and broken ribs. Or use the keelboat scan with planks removed.

issues.where: Coast: the four Name-stones (build5 nameStone :771)
issues.what: The name-lines are random rows of boxes. Lit, they read as an orange barcode or LED panel on the runestone; unlit, as black dashes (d-stone-keyx-lit, crops/thaleia-stone.png).
issues.fix: Draw runic name-lines into a small canvas texture (textures.js) and lay it as an emissive decal on the stone's face. Let the light come from inside the carved strokes, soft, with a faint glow halo, and leave the stone's scanned surface visible round it.

issues.where: Coast: the Fall shelf's Icemaw holes. Farlight: the Icemaw holes on the fields (2x2 L.sea cells)
issues.what: An Icemaw hole is a flat black polygon or square with straight facets on the grid, sitting in the ice like a black decal. It has no broken rim, slush, water sheen or bubbles (crops/fall-shelf-hole.png, d-f-maw).
issues.fix: Ring each hole with broken plates (floe shards from the pool), round its outline with the frayed band, and give the water inside a sheen and slow bubbles. Add a few cracks radiating into the ice (cracks stage 1-2 baked into tCrack round the hole).

issues.where: Coast and farlight: the sea-light fire cages, the cairns' cages and the tower tops (build5 fireCage :570, sealight :667)
issues.what: Seen from above or in a cine, the sea-light's fire is a small flame in an iron birdcage on top of a hollow tower whose open top shows as a stone ring. Unlit cairns are a ring of white low-poly chips round a black cage with a brown dish: toy-like.
issues.fix: Cap the ruined towers' tops with a platform and a broad iron brazier. Make the cairns from the base set's rock scans in the cliff stone (as rockPile does), not white dodecahedra. Make the cage thicker and soot it, with embers glowing in the dish while unlit but ready.

issues.where: Farlight: the Farthest Light's shaft (rime farLight scan)
issues.what: From the play camera the shaft's texture reads as birch bark (white with dark horizontal flecks), as the gate keeper noted. It also lacks weathering, snow on its ledges and rime on its windward side.
issues.fix: Re-grade the shaft's texture in pack-rime toward weathered grey stone with mortar lines at a larger scale, or use the towers' stone atlas. Add snow on the ledges and rime on the north side through the snow mask.

issues.where: Both zones: one-cell blocked footprints in thin ice (anchor, pole blocks, small rocks; gen5 footprints set them thick)
issues.what: Every small blocked footprint in thin ice becomes a thick-ice cell. It shows as a pale square tile with straight edges on the black ice under the prop (d-f-anchor, d-f-pole2). The sunken anchor, lit warm by the Cradle, reads as a small gold key or loot glyph.
issues.fix: Draw footprint cells standing in thin ice in the thin-ice look, with the prop's own ice collar (buildIce already covers footprints; the pale square comes from the thick snow look). Give the anchor snow and rime and sink it further, so it reads as dark iron.

issues.where: Coast: the jetty at high water
issues.what: At high tide the jetty stands over black water with a straight-edged pale vertical lip at the snow edge (the held water corner and the jetty's footprint). The boats drawn up beside it float over a dark rectangle (p-jetty-high).
issues.fix: Fray the deck's land edge, add pilings with ice collars at the waterline, and let the water meet the jetty's posts with foam.

issues.where: Both zones: the waypoint and the Landing's bare dark slab (build.js propMesh waypoint :2913, shared with other acts)
issues.what: On the snow, the waypoint's dark olive dodecagon slab and three standing stones read as an untextured toy, and the stones dither whenever the hero stands north of them (p-camp-unlit, e-fz-camp). In the Woods the same mesh sits on dark leaves and goes unnoticed.
issues.fix: In Act V zones, dust the slab and stones with snow (the cliff5 material with snow) and add a ring of ice crystals.

issues.where: Both zones: thin hairline seams across the ice and snow
issues.what: Faint dotted straight lines, one pixel wide, run across the ice and snow (whale strand, Fall shelf, farlight start). They are probably T-junction cracks between the band quads and the cell quads, or chunk joints, showing the darker pit beneath. This is a geometry issue, not a swiftshader one: T-junction cracks show on any rasteriser.
issues.fix: Weld the band and cell vertices (share corners) and close the T-junctions where the ice band meets 2-cell edges, or overdraw the ice 1 cm past the chunk edges. Confirm on a real GPU.

issues.where: Whitecliff after seaLit: the three sea-lights that answer on the northern horizon (world.js FAR_BEACONS :62-63, farFire :66; a request, since world.js is not ours)
issues.what: The design asks for "three new white sea-lights" flashing in a 12 s rhythm, "a lighthouse beam seen from far off" (design :197). Only the first (FAR_BEACONS[4]) has a colour (0xf0f4ff). [5] and [6] fall back to farFire's orange 0xffa040, so two of the three sea-lights are the same orange as the old war beacons (sampled at (207,169,102) and (86,73,53), against the white one's (207,212,227), p-town-north-cine). All of them are 7 m soft "dot" sprites with fog off, so on the phone they hang as big out-of-focus balls above the treeline rather than points on a horizon. At the play camera they are out of frame.
issues.fix: Request to world.js: give FAR_BEACONS[5] and [6] the same cold white as [4]. Shrink the sea-lights' sprites to 3-4 m with a hard bright core and a thin horizontal flare streak. On the 12 s flash, briefly stretch the streak sideways (the beam sweeping past) instead of only brightening the ball.
